title: Data Anomaly Detection & Quality Monitoring in Production

scenes.heading: Anomaly Detection
scenes.subheading: Catching bad data before consumers do
scenes.narration: Anomaly detection watches your data for unexpected changes so quality problems are caught before consumers ever see them.

scenes.heading: What to watch
bullets: Volume: row counts far above or below normal
Nulls: a spike in missing values
Freshness: data arriving late or not at all
scenes.narration: Volume anomalies catch dropped or duplicated loads when row counts jump or collapse. A sudden spike in null values often signals a broken upstream field. Distribution shifts reveal subtler corruption where totals look fine but values drifted. Duplicate keys break uniqueness assumptions, and freshness anomalies flag data that arrived late or not at all.

scenes.heading: Rule-based vs statistical checks
scenes.narration: Rule-based checks use fixed thresholds that are simple and explicit but break when data has natural seasonality or growth. Statistical or machine-learned checks learn what normal looks like and adapt to trends automatically. The trade-off is that adaptive checks are more powerful but harder to explain when they fire.

scenes.heading: A volume anomaly check
scenes.code:
-- Flag today's row count if it deviates > 30% from the
-- trailing 7-day average
WITH daily AS (
  SELECT load_date, COUNT(*) AS rows
  FROM fact_orders
  GROUP BY load_date
),
baseline AS (
  SELECT AVG(rows) AS avg_rows
  FROM daily
  WHERE load_date BETWEEN CURRENT_DATE - 7 AND CURRENT_DATE - 1
)
SELECT d.rows, b.avg_rows,
  ABS(d.rows - b.avg_rows) / b.avg_rows > 0.30 AS is_anomaly
FROM daily d, baseline b
WHERE d.load_date = CURRENT_DATE;
scenes.narration: This query compares today's row count against the trailing seven-day average as a dynamic baseline. If today deviates by more than thirty percent in either direction, it is flagged as an anomaly. Using a rolling baseline instead of a fixed number keeps the check honest as normal volumes grow over time.

scenes.text: Green pipelines can still ship wrong data. Quality monitoring watches the data itself, not just whether the job finished.
scenes.narration: A pipeline can finish green and still ship completely wrong data, which is why quality monitoring must watch the data itself and not merely whether the job completed.
